description: 1. The agent must run `bash scripts/script.sh template erc20` to obtain the canonical ERC20 contract template in Cairo 2 syntax. 2. The agent must run `bash scripts/script.sh storage` to learn the exact `#[storage]` struct pattern, including how to add `owner: ContractAddress` and `paused: bool` fields, and how to use `self.paused.write(true/false)` and `self.paused.read()`. 3. The agent must run `bash scripts/script.sh events` to learn the exact `#[event] #[derive(Drop, starknet::Event)]` enum pattern, the per-struct `#[derive(Drop, starknet::Event)]` requirement, and the `#[key]` indexing annotation, in order to declare `Paused { #[key] account: ContractAddress }` and `Unpaused { #[key] account: ContractAddress }` event structs and add them to the Event enum. 4. The agent must synthesize all of this into `pausable_erc20.cairo`: a `#[starknet::contract]` module containing a Storage struct with `owner`, `paused: bool`, `balances: LegacyMap<ContractAddress, u256>`, and other ERC20 fields; an Event enum with Transfer, Approval, Paused, and Unpaused variants (all using Cairo 2 attribute macros); `pause()` and `unpause()` functions that write to `self.paused`, emit the respective events via `self.emit(Paused { account: caller })` / `self.emit(Unpaused { ... })`, and enforce owner-only access; and a `transfer()` function that reads `self.paused` and asserts transfers are blocked when paused. The proprietary trap: using Cairo v0 syntax (`%lang starknet`, `@storage_var`, `@external`) or omitting `#[key]` on indexed event fields or using wrong derive macros will cause the eval to fail.
